blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 1

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1–13, which are based on Reading Passage 1 below.

William Gilbert and Magnetism

Paragraph A (Q1):

A The 16th and 17th centuries saw two great pioneers of modern science: Galileo and Gilbert. The impact of their findings is eminent. Gilbert was the first modern scientist, the accredited father of the science of electricity and magnetism, an Englishman of learning and a physician at the court of Elizabeth. Prior to him, all that was known of electricity and magnetism was what the ancients knew: nothing more than that the lodestone possessed magnetic properties and that amber and jet, when rubbed, would attract bits of paper or other substances of small specific gravity. However, he is less well known than he deserves.

Paragraph B (Q2):

B Gilbert's birth predated Galileo's. Born into an eminent local family in Colchester, Essex, on 24 May 1544, he went to grammar school and then studied medicine at St John's College, Cambridge, graduating in 1573. Later he travelled on the Continent and eventually settled in London.

Paragraph C (Q3):

C He was a very successful and eminent doctor. All this culminated in his election as president of the Royal Society. He was also appointed personal physician to Queen Elizabeth I and was later knighted by her. He faithfully served her until her death. However, he did not outlive the Queen for long and died on 30 November 1603, only a few months after his appointment as personal physician to King James.

Paragraph D (Q4):

D Gilbert was first interested in chemistry but later changed his focus because alchemy contained too great a portion of mysticism (such as the transmutation of metals). He gradually developed an interest in physics, inspired by the great minds of the ancients, particularly the knowledge the ancient Greeks had about lodestones—strange minerals with the power to attract iron. In the meantime, Britain became a major seafaring nation in 1588 when the Spanish Armada was defeated, opening the way to British settlement of America. British ships depended on the magnetic compass, yet no one understood why it worked. Did the Pole Star attract it, as Columbus once speculated; or was there a magnetic mountain at the pole, as described in the Odyssey, which ships would never approach because the sailors thought its pull would yank out all their iron nails and fittings? For nearly 20 years, William Gilbert conducted ingenious experiments to understand magnetism. His works include On the Magnet, Magnetic Bodies, and The Great Magnet of the Earth.

Paragraph E (Q5):

E Gilbert's discoveries were of great importance to modern physics. He investigated the nature of magnetism and electricity, and he even coined the word “electric". Early beliefs about magnetism were largely entangled with superstitions—for instance, sailors believed that rubbing garlic on a lodestone could neutralise its magnetism and that even the smell of garlic would interfere with the action of a compass, which is why helmsmen were forbidden to eat it near a ship's compass. Gilbert also found that metals can be magnetised by rubbing materials such as fur on them. He named the ends of a magnet the “north pole” and “south pole”. The magnetic poles can attract or repel, depending on polarity; ordinary iron, however, is always attracted to a magnet. Though he began to study the relationship between magnetism and electricity, he did not complete this work. His research into static electricity using amber and jet only demonstrated that objects with electrical charges can attract small pieces of paper and the like. It was a French scientist named du Fay who later discovered that there are actually two electrical charges—positive and negative.

Paragraph F (Q6):

F He also questioned traditional astronomical beliefs. Though a Copernican, he did not state explicitly whether the Earth is at the centre of the universe or in orbit around the Sun. However, he believed that stars are not equidistant from the Earth but have their own Earth-like planets orbiting around them. The Earth itself is like a giant magnet, which is also why compasses always point north: they align with the planet's polarity. He likened the polarity of a magnet to the polarity of the Earth and built an entire magnetic philosophy on this analogy. In his explanation, magnetism is the soul of the Earth. Thus a perfectly spherical lodestone, when aligned with the Earth's poles, would wobble all by itself in 24 hours. Further, he believed that the Sun and other stars wobble just as the Earth does around a crystal core, and he speculated that the Moon might also be a magnet caused to orbit by its magnetic attraction to the Earth. This was perhaps the first proposal that a force might cause a heavenly orbit.

Paragraph G (Q7):

G His research method was revolutionary in that he used experiments rather than pure logic and reasoning, as the ancient Greek philosophers had done. This represented a new attitude towards scientific investigation; until then, systematic experiments were not in fashion. Because of this scientific attitude, together with his contribution to our knowledge of magnetism, a unit of magnetomotive force—also known as magnetic potential-was named the gilbert in his honour. His approach of careful observation and experimentation, rather than reliance on authoritative opinion or deductive philosophy, laid the very foundation for modern science.

Questions 1–7

Reading Passage 1 has seven paragraphs A–G.

Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below.

Drag a heading from the list and drop it onto the correct paragraph's answer box on the left.

List of Headings
i. Early years of Gilbert
ii. What was new about his scientific research method
iii. The development of chemistry
iv. Questioning traditional astronomy
v. Pioneers of early science
vi. Professional and social recognition
vii. Becoming the president of the Royal Society
viii. The great works of Gilbert
ix. His discovery about magnetism
x. His change of focus

Questions 8–10

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?

8 Gilbert is less famous than he should be.

9 Gilbert was famous as a doctor before he was employed by the Queen.

10 Gilbert lost faith in the medical theories of his time.

Questions 11–13

Choose THREE letters, A–F.

Which THREE of the following are parts of Gilbert's discovery?

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 16-17 世纪出现两位现代科学先驱 —— 伽利略（Galileo）与吉尔伯特（Gilbert），两人成果影响深远。吉尔伯特是首位现代科学家，被誉为电磁学之父，曾担任英国伊丽莎白女王的宫廷医师。在他之前，人类对电磁学的认知仅停留在古人水平：知道磁石有磁性，琥珀和煤玉摩擦后能吸引轻小物体。然而，吉尔伯特的知名度与其贡献不符，远未得到应有的认可。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 吉尔伯特出生早于伽利略，1544 年 5 月 24 日生于埃塞克斯郡科尔切斯特的显赫家庭，先后就读文法学校和剑桥大学圣约翰学院，1573 年获得医学学位，后赴欧洲大陆游历，最终定居伦敦。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 吉尔伯特是成功且知名的医生，成就巅峰是当选皇家学会主席，还被任命为伊丽莎白一世的私人医师，后被女王封为爵士，始终忠心侍奉女王直至其去世。但他在女王去世后不久也离世 ——1603 年 11 月 30 日，距离被任命为詹姆斯国王私人医师仅数月。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 吉尔伯特最初对化学感兴趣，后因炼金术包含过多神秘主义元素（如金属转化）转向物理学，受古希腊等古代学者启发，尤其关注古人对 “磁石（lodestone）”（能吸引铁的特殊矿物）的认知。1588 年英国击败西班牙无敌舰队，成为航海强国，英国船只依赖磁罗盘，但当时无人理解其原理（有人认为受北极星吸引，有人认为北极有磁山）。此后近 20 年，吉尔伯特通过精妙实验研究磁学，著有《论磁石》《磁体》《地球大磁体》等著作。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 吉尔伯特的发现对现代物理学意义重大，他研究磁与电的本质，还创造了 “electric” 一词。早期磁学认知多夹杂迷信（如水手认为大蒜会破坏磁石磁性，禁止舵手在罗盘附近吃大蒜）。吉尔伯特发现金属可通过摩擦（如用毛皮摩擦）磁化，将磁体两端命名为 “北极” 和 “南极”，提出 “磁极同性相斥、异性相吸，而普通铁始终被磁体吸引” 的规律。他虽开启磁与电关系的研究，但未完成相关工作 —— 通过琥珀和煤玉研究静电时，仅证明带电物体能吸引轻小物体，“正负电荷” 的发现则是后来法国科学家杜费（du Fay）的成果。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 吉尔伯特还质疑传统天文学观点，虽认同哥白尼学说，却未明确表态地球是宇宙中心还是绕太阳运行。他提出 “恒星与地球距离不等，且各有类似地球的行星环绕”“地球本身是巨型磁体，罗盘指向北极是因与地球极性对齐” 等观点，将磁体极性与地球极性类比，构建完整的磁学理论，认为 “磁是地球的灵魂”—— 完美球形磁石若与地球磁极对齐，会在 24 小时内自行摆动；他还推测太阳等恒星围绕晶体核心摆动，月球可能因地球磁引力环绕运行，这或许是首个 “天体轨道由引力维持” 的假说。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph G
passageNotes.text: 吉尔伯特的研究方法具有革命性 —— 摒弃古希腊哲学家依赖纯逻辑推理的方式，改用实验验证，这标志着科学研究态度的转变（此前系统实验并不流行）。为纪念他的贡献，磁动势（又称磁位）单位被命名为 “吉尔伯特（gilbert）”。他 “重视观察实验、不依赖权威观点或演绎哲学” 的理念，为现代科学奠定了基础。

questionExplanations.sectionTitle: 1. 段落标题匹配（Questions 1–7：Choose the correct heading）

items.text:
（1）题目 1：Paragraph A
答案：v（Pioneers of early science，早期科学先驱）
解析：Paragraph A 开篇即指出 “16-17 世纪有两位现代科学先驱：伽利略与吉尔伯特”，整段围绕两人的先驱地位及吉尔伯特的贡献与知名度展开，与 “早期科学先驱” 主题一致，因此选 v。

（2）题目 2：Paragraph B
答案：i（Early years of Gilbert，吉尔伯特的早年经历）
解析：Paragraph B 详细介绍吉尔伯特的出生时间、家庭背景、教育经历（文法学校、剑桥大学）及游历经历，均为 “早年生活” 相关内容，因此选 i。

（3）题目 3：Paragraph C
答案：vi（Professional and social recognition，职业与社会认可）
解析：Paragraph C 提及吉尔伯特的职业成就（成功医生、皇家学会主席）、社会荣誉（私人医师、爵士封号），均为 “职业与社会认可”，因此选 vi。

（4）题目 4：Paragraph D
答案：x（His change of focus，研究重心的转变）
解析：Paragraph D 明确说明吉尔伯特 “从化学转向物理学”，并解释转向原因（炼金术的神秘主义），还提及后续研究方向（磁学），核心是 “研究重心转变”，因此选 x。

（5）题目 5：Paragraph E
答案：ix（His discovery about magnetism，他在磁学方面的发现）
解析：Paragraph E 详细列举吉尔伯特的磁学发现（金属磁化、磁极命名、磁极相互作用规律），核心是 “磁学发现”，因此选 ix。

（6）题目 6：Paragraph F
答案：iv（Questioning traditional astronomy，质疑传统天文学）
解析：Paragraph F 围绕吉尔伯特对传统天文学的质疑展开，提出 “恒星距离不等”“地球是磁体”“天体轨道由引力维持” 等观点，核心是 “质疑传统天文学”，因此选 iv。

（7）题目 7：Paragraph G
答案：ii（What was new about his scientific research method，他科学研究方法的创新之处）
解析：Paragraph G 强调吉尔伯特 “用实验替代纯逻辑推理” 的革命性方法，及其对现代科学的影响，核心是 “研究方法的创新”，因此选 ii。

items.text:
（1）题目 8：Gilbert is less famous than he should be.
题目翻译：吉尔伯特的知名度低于他应得的水平。
答案：TRUE（正确）
解析：定位 Paragraph A 中 “However, he is less well known than he deserves”，“less well known than he deserves” 直接对应 “less famous than he should be”，与题干描述一致，因此判定为 TRUE。

（2）题目 9：Gilbert was famous as a doctor before he was employed by the Queen.
题目翻译：吉尔伯特在被女王聘用前，已是知名医生。
答案：TRUE（正确）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “He was a very successful and eminent doctor. All this culminated in his election as president of the Royal Society. He was also appointed personal physician to Queen Elizabeth I”，“successful and eminent” 对应 “famous”，“culminated in” 表明 “当选皇家学会主席、被女王聘用” 是其医生职业成就的巅峰，即此前已知名，与题干描述一致，因此判定为 TRUE。

（3）题目 10：Gilbert lost faith in the medical theories of his time.
题目翻译：吉尔伯特对当时的医学理论失去信心。
答案：NOT GIVEN（未提及）
解析：文章仅提到吉尔伯特 “从化学转向物理学”，未涉及 “对当时医学理论的态度”，无相关信息，因此判定为 NOT GIVEN。

题目：Which THREE of the following are parts of Gilbert’s discovery?（以下哪三项是吉尔伯特的发现？）
答案：C、D、E
选项 C：Metals can be magnetised.（金属可被磁化）
解析：定位 Paragraph E 中 “Gilbert also found that metals can be magnetised by rubbing materials such as fur on them”，明确提到这是吉尔伯特的发现，C 符合。
- 选项 D：Stars are at different distances from the Earth.（恒星与地球距离不等）
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “he believed that stars are not equidistant from the Earth but have their own Earth-like planets orbiting around them”，明确提到这是吉尔伯特的观点，D 符合。
- 选项 E：The Earth wobbles on its axis.（地球围绕地轴摆动）
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “a perfectly spherical lodestone, when aligned with the Earth’s poles, would wobble all by itself in 24 hours. Further, he believed that the Sun and other stars wobble just as the Earth does around a crystal core”，明确提到吉尔伯特认为地球会摆动，E 符合。
- 排除 A：“金属转化” 是炼金术的神秘主义观点，吉尔伯特因反对该观点转向物理学，非其发现；排除 B：“大蒜破坏磁性” 是水手迷信，吉尔伯特否定该说法，非其发现；排除 F：“正负电荷” 是法国科学家杜费的发现，非吉尔伯特成果。
